mainTopic: Saying זמן (שהחיינו) on שמיני עצרת, whether it needs a כוס, and whether רבי יהודה requires לינה on שמיני; the final ruling follows רב נחמן.
overview: The גמרא tries to use a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן, who says we recite זמן (שהחיינו) on שמיני עצרת. The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא's 'blessing' may just mean mentioning the day in ברכת המזון and תפלה. Along the way the גמרא asks whether זמן needs a cup of wine. It tries to support רב נחמן, who says זמן can be said even in the marketplace, but that proof is also pushed off. Next the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really holds that שמיני requires לינה, since his own six-day rule seems to exclude it. It answers that the rule only excludes פסח שני. It tries to back this up from a משנה about ביכורים, but that משנה might follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who learns waving through a גזירה שוה from שלמים. Finally, רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about זמן on שמיני. The הלכה follows רב נחמן: we say זמן. A supporting ברייתא begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Suggesting the ברייתא means the blessing of זמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the 'blessing' mentioned in the ברייתא is ברכת זמן, which would support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean the blessing of זמן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא it just quoted and suggests that its 'blessing' means שהחיינו. That would support רבי יוחנן, who says we say זמן on שמיני עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says שמיני has its own separate blessing. If 'blessing' means זמן, then שמיני gets its own שהחיינו, just as רבי יוחנן says.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that...?' A formula that offers a reading as a proof
The blessing of שהחיינו, said at the start of a יום טוב

phrases.english: What, is it not the blessing of 'time'?
phrases.notes: Suggests a proof for רבי יוחנן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן's ruling about זמן on שמיני עצרת
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that זמן is said on שמיני עצרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that says שמיני has its own blessing

steps.title: No, it means ברכת המזון and תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The 'blessing' may mean mentioning שמיני עצרת in ברכת המזון and in תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means ברכת המזון and תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא could simply mean that on שמיני we mention שמיני עצרת, not סוכות, in bentching and davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'blessing' means the text of ברכת המזון and תפלה, the ברייתא says nothing about שהחיינו. So רבי יוחנן gets no support from it.

phrases.english: No, it means Grace after Meals and prayer.
phrases.notes: The point is mentioning the day by its own name in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of 'blessing' as זמן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'blessing' can mean the mention of the day in bentching and davening

steps.title: Support: זמן is not said all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the rejection. The ברייתא speaks of all seven days, and זמן is not said all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense. If you thought it means זמן, is there a זמן on all seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the rejection in step 2. The ברייתא refers to a blessing on all seven days of סוכות, and שהחיינו is not said every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת המזון and תפלה do mention the יום טוב every day. שהחיינו is only said on the first day. So the ברייתא's 'all seven days' fits ברכת המזון and תפלה better.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So too it is logical.' Introduces support for the last position
'It would enter your mind' — if you were to think

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if it entered your mind that it means 'time',
is there a blessing of 'time' all seven days?
phrases.notes: שהחיינו is said only on the first day

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the rejection in step 2
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא means ברכת המזון and תפלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: זמן is not recited on all seven days

steps.title: זמן can be made up on a later day
steps.stepSummary: The support is rejected. If someone missed זמן on the first day, he can say it on any later day, so 'all seven' can fit זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. If he did not bless today, he blesses tomorrow or another day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the support from step 3. 'All seven days' can mean that a person who forgot שהחיינו can still say it on any day of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא may not mean זמן is said every day. It may mean זמן can be said on any day if it was missed. So the reading of זמן is possible again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is not difficult.' Deflects an argument

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean זמן is said every day of סוכות. It means a person who missed it can still say it later in the חג.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
for if he did not recite the blessing today,
he recites it tomorrow, or on another day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that 'all seven days' cannot refer to זמן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'All seven' can mean זמן may be made up on any day

steps.title: But זמן needs a cup of wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the make-up idea. זמן requires a כוס, and wine is not always available on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, we require a cup!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to step 4. If זמן needs a cup of wine, how can someone just say it on any random day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that שהחיינו is said over wine, as in קידוש. A person may not have wine on a weekday of the חג. So making up זמן on any day seems hard.

phrases.english: In any case, we require a cup!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the make-up answer of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that זמן can be said on any later day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: זמן requires wine, and wine is not available every day

steps.title: Support for רב נחמן: זמן even in the market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא supports רב נחמן, who holds זמן can be said anywhere, without a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רב נחמן? רב נחמן said: one may say זמן even in the marketplace. For if you say we need a cup, is there a cup every day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question from step 5 into a proof. Since the ברייתא allows זמן on any day, it must not need wine, just as רב נחמן says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If זמן required a כוס, the ברייתא could not casually allow it on any day. That suggests no cup is needed, which is רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say it supports him?' Offers a proof

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rav Nachman,
for Rav Nachman said:
One says 'time' even in the marketplace.
For if you say we need a cup,
is there a cup every day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the problem of step 5 as a proof for רב נחמן
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that זמן does not need a כוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא as explained in step 4

steps.title: Maybe he happened to have a cup
steps.stepSummary: The proof for רב נחמן is rejected. The ברייתא may speak of a case where wine happened to be available.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a cup happened to come his way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof for רב נחמן. Maybe the ברייתא means that if the person happens to get wine on a later day, he can say זמן then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not have to mean no cup is needed. It can mean he says זמן when a cup becomes available. So it does not prove רב נחמן's view.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves neither רבי יוחנן's view about זמן on שמיני, nor רב נחמן's view that זמן needs no cup. Every proof was pushed off.

phrases.english: Perhaps a cup happened to come his way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof for רב נחמן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could refer to a case where a cup happened to be available

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה hold שמיני requires לינה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יהודה's view that שמיני requires לינה. It quotes another ברייתא of his, which says only a festival followed by six days requires לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that שמיני requires staying overnight? But it was taught: רבי יהודה says, from where do we know that פסח שני does not require staying overnight? As it says: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents,' and it is written: 'Six days you shall eat מצות.' Whatever requires six days requires staying overnight; whatever does not require six days does not require staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יהודה's view in the earlier ברייתא. It brings a different ברייתא in his name and sets up a contradiction, which is finished in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns from two verses next to each other that לינה goes together with having six more days of the חג. פסח שני has no six days after it, so it needs no לינה. This rule will soon be applied to שמיני.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying overnight in ירושלים after bringing the קרבן
The make-up קרבן פסח on 14 אייר
'But wasn't it taught?' Brings a contradicting ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Six' here does not mean the six days before שמיני. It means a festival that has six more days of observance after the overnight stay, like פסח.

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שְׁמִינִי טָעוּן לִינָה?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that the Eighth Day requires staying overnight?
But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְפֶסַח שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ טָעוּן לִינָה —
phrases.english: From where do we know that the second Pesach does not require staying overnight?
As it says: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents,'
phrases.notes: This is דברים טז:ז, the source for staying overnight (לינה).

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Six days you shall eat matzos.'
phrases.notes: This is דברים טז:ח, the very next verse.

phrases.english: That which requires six days requires staying overnight;

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ טָעוּן שִׁשָּׁה — אֵינוֹ טָעוּן לִינָה.
phrases.english: that which does not require six days does not require staying overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שְׁמִינִי טָעוּן לִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: רבי יהודה's view on לינה for שמיני
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that שמיני requires לינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own ברייתא ties לינה to festivals followed by six days

steps.title: The rule excludes שמיני too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge. The six-day rule should also exclude שמיני, so רבי יהודה contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it come to exclude? Is it not to exclude the eighth day of the חג as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the contradiction from step 8. The six-day rule seems to exclude שמיני, which has no six days after it, from לינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יהודה's rule, שמיני should not require לינה. That clashes with the earlier ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says שמיני does require לינה. The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighth day of סוכות, שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: What does it come to exclude?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי נָמֵי שְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג?
phrases.english: Is it not to exclude the eighth day of the Festival as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that שמיני requires לינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The six-day rule, which excludes פסח שני, should also exclude שמיני

steps.title: The six-day rule excludes only פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's six-day rule does not exclude שמיני. It excludes פסח שני, which is similar to the first פסח but is not followed by six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The rule comes to exclude פסח שני, which is like the first פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 9. It explains that the six-day rule was meant to exclude a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'only a festival followed by six days' do not come to exclude שמיני. They exclude פסח שני. It has a קרבן just like the first פסח, so we might think it also requires לינה. Since no six days follow it, it does not. So רבי יהודה can still hold that שמיני requires לינה, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'second פסח', a make-up offering one month later for those who missed the first

steps.confusionAlert: The six-day rule is not a list of every case without לינה. It only targets a case that could look similar to the first פסח, namely פסח שני.

phrases.english: No, it comes to exclude
the second Pesach, which is like it (the first Pesach)
phrases.notes: Like the first פסח in having a קרבן, but without six days of festival after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the self-contradiction raised in Steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the purpose of an exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The six-day rule excludes every festival without six days after it, including שמיני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The six-day rule only excludes פסח שני. שמיני can still require לינה.

steps.title: Support from the ביכורים משנה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says ביכורים require תנופה and לינה. Since the view requiring תנופה is רבי יהודה's, he requires לינה even without a festival of six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, as we learned in a משנה: ביכורים require a קרבן, song, waving, and staying overnight. Who do we know says waving? רבי יהודה. And the משנה says it requires staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer in Step 10. It shows that רבי יהודה requires לינה even where no six-day festival follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים are not tied to a six-day festival, yet the משנה requires לינה for them. If this משנה follows רבי יהודה, then his six-day rule cannot be a total rule excluding everything else. It must only be excluding פסח שני, as Step 10 said.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces a supporting proof)
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Waving (moving the offering back and forth before the altar)

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
as we learned in a Mishnah: First fruits require
an offering, song, waving, and staying overnight.
Whom have you heard
who says waving? Rabbi Yehuda,
and it says: it requires staying overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's six-day rule only excludes פסח שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requiring קרבן, שיר, תנופה and לינה for ביכורים, attributed to רבי יהודה because of the תנופה

steps.title: Source that רבי יהודה requires waving for ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה reads 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' as waving, because the setting down is already written in a different verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה says, 'And you shall set it down' means waving. Do you say it means waving, or perhaps only actually setting it down? When the Torah says 'and he shall set it down', setting down is already stated. So how do I explain 'And you shall set it down'? It means waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim from Step 11 that רבי יהודה is the one who requires תנופה for ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah mentions setting down the basket twice. One verse, 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ', already covers the actual setting down. So רבי יהודה says the second verse, 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ', must teach something new: waving.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall set it down' (דברים כו:י)
'And he shall set it down' (דברים כו:ד)

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'And you shall set it down' — this is waving.
Do you say this is waving,
or perhaps it is only actual setting down?
When it says 'and he shall set it down,'
setting down is already stated.
So how do I explain 'and you shall set it down'?
This is waving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the assumption in Step 11 that the תנופה view belongs to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds ביכורים require תנופה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה reads 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ' as waving, since 'וְהִנִּיחוֹ' already covers setting down

steps.title: Maybe the ביכורים משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב also requires תנופה for ביכורים, so the משנה may follow him and not רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. As it was taught: 'And the כהן shall take the basket from your hand' teaches that ביכורים require waving. These are the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens the proof from Step 11. Another תנא also holds of תנופה, so the משנה cannot be pinned on רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 11 depended on רבי יהודה being the only one who requires תנופה. Since רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires it too, the משנה could be his. Then it tells us nothing about רבי יהודה's view on לינה.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא,
phrases.english: But perhaps it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
as it was taught: 'And the priest shall take the basket from your hand' —
this taught regarding first fruits
that they require waving,
the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attribution of the משנה to רבי יהודה made in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ביכורים משנה. The answer of Step 10 itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed only רבי יהודה holds of תנופה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds it too.

steps.title: How does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn waving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the verse about taking the basket teaches waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question. The verse only says the כהן takes the basket, so where does waving come from? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It asks for the source behind the view just quoted, since the plain words of the verse do not mention waving.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view quoted in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse 'וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן הַטֶּנֶא מִיָּדֶךָ' teaches waving

steps.title: The word 'hand' links ביכורים to שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving through a גזירה שוה. The word 'יד' appears by ביכורים and by שלמים, and שלמים require waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'יד' and 'יד' of שלמים. It is written here: 'And the כהן shall take the basket from your hand', and it is written there: 'His own hands shall bring the fire-offerings of ה'.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 14. It links the word 'hand' in the ביכורים verse to the word 'hands' in the שלמים verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about שלמים uses 'hands' and then goes on to require waving the breast. Because the same word 'hand' appears by ביכורים, the waving rule is carried over to ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A derivation from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Two תנאים require תנופה for ביכורים: רבי יהודה, from the extra 'וְהִנַּחְתּוֹ', and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, from the 'יד-יד' link to שלמים. So the ביכורים משנה cannot prove רבי יהודה's view on לינה for sure.

phrases.english: It is derived from 'hand' and 'hand' of peace-offerings,
it is written here: 'And the priest shall take the basket from your hand,'
and it is written there:
'His own hands shall bring the fire-offerings of the Lord.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:ל, which goes on to require waving the breast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'יד' from שלמים, which require waving, teaches that ביכורים require waving too.

steps.title: Both the priest and the owner wave together
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה of 'יד' works in both directions. Because a כהן takes part with ביכורים, a כהן also takes part in waving שלמים. Because the בעלים take part with שלמים, the בעלים also take part in waving ביכורים. So both must take part: the כהן puts his hand under the owner's hand and waves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as here (ביכורים) a priest is involved, so too there (שלמים) a priest is involved. And just as there (שלמים) the owner is involved, so too here (ביכורים) the owner is involved. How does that work? The priest puts his hand under the owner's hand and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the גזירה שוה of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It shows that the כהן and the owner wave the ביכורים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יד' links ביכורים and שלמים, so each one takes on a detail from the other. ביכורים give the 'כהן' detail to שלמים, and שלמים give the 'בעלים' detail to ביכורים. This also completes the pushback from Step 13: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב clearly requires תנופה, so the משנה might follow him, and it is no proof for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the offering or of the ביכורים
How so? How do both fit together?

steps.whatToRemember: For ביכורים (according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), the כהן puts his hand under the owner's hand and they wave together. This means the משנה requiring תנופה is not necessarily רבי יהודה's view.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כאן' (here) means ביכורים, and 'להלן' (there) means שלמים. Each side borrows one detail from the other. It is not a one-way comparison.

phrases.english: Just as here (ביכורים) — a priest,
phrases.notes: With ביכורים the basket is taken 'from your hand' by the כהן.

phrases.english: so too there (שלמים) — a priest.
And just as there (שלמים) — the owner,
phrases.notes: 'His hands shall bring' refers to the owner of the שלמים.

phrases.english: so too here (ביכורים) — the owner.
How so?
The priest places his hand
under the owner's hand and waves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כָּאן — כֹּהֵן, אַף לְהַלָּן — כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גזירה שוה begun in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse teaches waving for ביכורים (from Step 14)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזירה שוה of 'יד' teaches that the כהן and the בעלים wave together, with the כהן's hand under the owner's hand.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the proofs have been pushed aside, the גמרא asks what the final conclusion is about saying זמן on שמיני של חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for the bottom-line ruling on the larger question of saying זמן on שמיני של חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attempts to prove the זמן question from the ברייתא (steps 1-7) were all pushed off. The רבי יהודה discussion in between was about לינה, not זמן. So the גמרא now returns to the זמן question and asks directly what the practical ruling is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion on it? (asking for the final ruling)

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the לינה digression about רבי יהודה ends, the גמרא returns to the זמן question from steps 1-7 and asks for the final ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one says זמן (שהחיינו) on שמיני של חג

steps.title: Two views on saying זמן on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that one says זמן on שמיני של חג. רב שֵׁשֶׁת rules that one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: we say the זמן blessing on the eighth day of the festival. רב שֵׁשֶׁת said: we do not say the זמן blessing on the eighth day of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two opposing rulings from two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treats שמיני עצרת as its own new festival, so it deserves its own שהחיינו. רב שֵׁשֶׁת treats it as tied to סוכות, so the זמן said on the first day of סוכות already covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: The שהחיינו blessing said on a new festival
The eighth day of סוכות (שמיני עצרת)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
One recites the blessing of time on the eighth day of the festival,
and Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים זְמַן בִּשְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: One does not recite the blessing of time on the eighth day of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אוֹמְרִים זְמַן בִּשְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the competing answers to the question in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: say זמן on שמיני של חג. רב שֵׁשֶׁת: do not.

steps.title: The הלכה: we say זמן on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב נחמן: one says זמן on שמיני של חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we say the זמן blessing on the eighth day of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument and rules like רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the practical bottom line of the whole discussion. שמיני עצרת counts as a new festival for the blessing of זמן, so שהחיינו is said on it.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: we say שהחיינו (זמן) on שמיני עצרת, following רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why שהחיינו is said in קידוש and candle lighting on שמיני עצרת to this day.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא: אוֹמְרִים זְמַן בִּשְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: And the halakha is: one recites the blessing of time on the eighth day of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: אוֹמְרִים זְמַן בִּשְׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב נחמן: זמן is said on שמיני של חג.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that agrees with רב נחמן. It opens with the word 'שמיני' and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רב נחמן: The eighth day...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to bring a ברייתא that backs up רב נחמן's ruling, and the ברייתא continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ruling like רב נחמן, the גמרא adds support from a תנאי source. The full content of the ברייתא comes on the next עמוד.
